title: Lenovo relaunches ultra-wide monitor with 140 W USB-C charging, 2.5 GbE and cheaper pricing
text:
Lenovo has quietly started selling its ThinkVision P40WD-40 monitor at a reduced price. For context, the company introduced the 39.7-inch monitor over a year ago during IFA 2025. At the time, Lenovo claimed that the monitor would retail for $2,182 in the US upon arriving in November 2025.

For some reason, the ThinkVision P40WD-40 seemingly disappeared around May 2026 from Lenovo's website. Now, it has returned for $1,286.59, a 41% reduction on its original MSRP. Better still, Walmart is selling the same monitor for $899. As a result, the ThinkVision P40WD-40 is now cheaper than equivalent options like the Dell UltraSharp U4025QW (curr. $1,394 on Amazon).

...

In summary, the ThinkVision P40WD-40 outputs at 5,120 x 2,160 pixels (5K2K) across its 39.7-inch and 2500R curved IPS display. Featuring 400 nits peak brightness, the monitor also offers a 24-120 Hz variable refresh rate, 98% DCI-P3 colour space coverage and 10-bit colour depth (8-bit + FRC). Moreover, Lenovo has applied an anti-glare coating to complement its relatively thin bezels.

The ThinkVision P40WD-40 is not shy of ports, either. As the image below shows, the monitor contains three USB ports on its front side, which can be hidden when needed. Meanwhile, the back of the monitor hides another four USB Type-A ports, 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet and Thunderbolt 4. Incidentally, the latter can charge a connected device at up to 140 W. Please see Lenovo's website for more details about the ThinkVision P40WD-40.

title: Flanders Scientific | VP and V Series Monitors
text:
Flanders Scientific | VP and V Series Monitors

Nov 5, 2026

## 7 New Additions to the FSI Monitor Lineup

Today we're announcing seven new additions to our QD-OLED monitor offerings across two new product lines, the VP Series and V Series. These new units use the same exceptional panels as the XMP and XMP C series, with the same calibration and analyzer capabilities, but with a more focused feature set that substantially lowers the cost.

Bram Desmet and Peter Barber explain the VP and V Series

XMP and XMP C continue as our flagship, more feature-rich reference monitors and remain in full production, while VP and V deliver the same image quality for workflows that don't need everything XMP offers, at a much lower price.

## VP Series — VP270 · VP310 · VP551 · VP651

This series was designed with the post house in mind: environments where professional inputs and color accuracy are paramount, but where users typically rely on a standalone scope solution and don't need processed monitor outputs or on-monitor Look LUT support.

By removing features not typically needed in post, these units can be made far more affordable, up to 30% less than their XMP counterparts, without compromising the core requirements of a color-critical environment.

We also took the opportunity with this new hardware platform to add something the XMP series lacked: optional 3D support. It's a niche requirement, but few professional monitoring solutions support 3D, so there is real demand that we want to address.

Beyond the post house, the VP Series is a great fit for any application that doesn't need the extended feature set of XMP and XMP C series monitors, but wants the same level of image quality.

VP Series highlights

Professional SDI connectivity for post and broadcast, with onboard HDMI and DisplayPort for secondary use cases.

- Same QD-OLED panels as the matching XMP models
- 4× 12G-SDI inputs with clean SDI outputs
- HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4 inputs
- 120 Hz refresh and stereo 3D support, with optional active 3D glasses system
- Quad input support with independent color configuration per input/quadrant
- Core FSI feature set: GaiaColor AutoCal, GaiaColor Analyzer, HDR and SDR LUM Coloring exposure check (false color), custom markers, and red/green/blue-only modes

## V Series — V270 · V310 · V550

This series complements our other QD-OLED solutions for applications that don't require professional SDI connectivity. Equipped with HDMI and DisplayPort, these units offer the same panels and performance as their XMP counterparts at a much lower cost, up to 48% less.

The idea is an ecosystem where a facility can run XMP or VP units in its primary grading suites and V Series units in complementary rooms that don't need SDI: VFX, editorial, or audio post, for example.

The V Series is also a far lower-priced entry point for colorists working over HDMI or DisplayPort and not over SDI.

V Series highlights

HDMI and DisplayPort inputs for VFX, animation, game development, and any environment, including some grading suites, where SDI isn't part of the signal chain. 

- Same QD-OLED panels as the matching XMP models

- Core FSI feature set: GaiaColor AutoCal, GaiaColor Analyzer, HDR and SDR LUM Coloring exposure check (false color), custom markers, and red/green/blue-only modes 
- Lowest cost of entry to FSI QD-OLED

title: PRISM+ Goes All White With Its New U Series Monitors - NYLON
text:
# PRISM+ Goes All White With Its New U Series Monitors

- Nov 12, 2026

Singapore display brand PRISM+ has launched the U Series, its first range of pure-white monitors, aimed at people who want a screen that suits a minimalist desk, particularly one with a Mac on it. The company says nearly four in ten desktop visitors to its website use a Mac, yet most of its monitors looked like they belonged in a gaming or office setup.

The six-model range runs in tiers:

- PRO (U270 PRO, U320 PRO): 144Hz QHD panels for everyday work and casual gaming, with the 27-inch U270 PRO starting at S$269.
- Ultra (U270, U320, U370): 4K screens in 27-, 31.5- and 37-inch sizes with single-cable USB-C, which carries picture, data and 65W of laptop charging.
- U320 6K: the flagship, a 31.5-inch 6K display for creative work. A quantum dot film widens its colour range, and it’s factory-calibrated for accuracy. At 215 PPI, its pixel density suits macOS text scaling.

Summary of specs:

Every model has a white chassis and stand, a thin bezel on three sides, HDR400, a flicker-free backlight and low blue light settings. The 32-inch models and the U370 also include an ambient light sensor. A new on-screen menu adds picture enhancement, one-step scene presets for films, games and reading, and game-assist tools.

Pre-orders open on PRISM+’s website and its official Shopee store from 12 to 13 November. The U320 6K and U270 PRO will be on show at The Tech Show, booth 8111, from 13 to 15 November, and the U270 and U370 Ultra follow at the end of the month. Prices start from $299 (before promos).

# AOC launches U32U4 4K 120Hz monitor with Samsung’s five-layer QD-OLED panel for $975

AOC has launched another 32-inch 4K QD-OLED monitor in China.

Yesterday, 16:30 GMT•WhyCry•2 min read Comments

## AOC U32U4 arrives in China with Penta Tandem QD-OLED technology

AOC has launched the U32U4, a 31.5-inch monitor featuring Samsung Display’s Penta Tandem QD-OLED panel. The display offers 4K resolution at 120Hz and is now available in China for approximately $975. The new model focuses on color accuracy and connectivity rather than the higher refresh rates typically offered by gaming monitors.

The U32U4 uses Samsung’s five-layer QD-OLED technology, also referred to as EL Gen.3. This panel structure is designed to improve brightness and operating efficiency. AOC claims a peak HDR brightness of 1,000 nits, a 1,500,000:1 contrast ratio and a 0.03ms gray-to-gray response time.

...

The panel supports native 10-bit color and covers 99% of the DCI-P3 color space. AOC also advertises factory calibration with Delta E below 1, along with an anti-reflective coating intended to reduce reflections in brighter environments. The monitor supports Adaptive-Sync for gaming, although its 120Hz refresh rate is lower than that of many current 4K OLED gaming displays.

text:
MSI MAG 321UPX18 QD-OLED monitor priced at around $598 in China – PC Central

# MSI MAG 321UPX18 QD-OLED monitor priced at around $598 in China

MSI launches the MAG 321UPX18, a 31.5- inch 4K QD- OLED gaming monitor with 180Hz refresh rate and 0.03ms response time, priced at around $598 in China.

 By Oliver Grant 

 Published Nov 11, 2026 8:23 PM 

MSI just released a high-refresh 4K QD-OLED monitor which is surprisingly cheaper than the common price tag of this kind of panel. The new monitor MAG 321UPX18 aims at gamers looking for OLED responsiveness at cheaper prices compared to the usually high prices of 31.5" panels. MSI is presenting a more cost-effective solution to access OLED high-refresh gaming.

The MSI MAG 321UPX18 features a 31.5-inch QD-OLED panel.

## MSI launches a 31.5-inch 4K QD-OLED gaming monitor with 180Hz refresh rate and dual HDMI 2.1 ports

The monitor comes with a 31.5" QD-OLED panel offering a 3840 x 2160 resolution with 180 Hz refresh rate. To keep the action as smooth as possible, MSI chose a 0.03ms gray-to-gray response time for this panel. This is a 10-bit color display that provides deep gradients and precise shading for an immersive gaming and creation experience.

...

To offer the maximum connectivity options, this monitor has two HDMI 2.1 and one DisplayPort 1.4a. For even more connectivity, this display comes with a USB-C port. This port supports up to 15W power delivery in addition to data transfer. G-SYNC Compatible (NVIDIA) and FreeSync Premium Pro (AMD) features are supported for a tear-free experience.

The MAG 321UPX18 is priced at 3999 CNY (that's about $598 if you do the conversion). This price tag includes a 3 years replacement warranty as well as some burn-in protection functions. The new monitor is available for the Chinese market right now.

With this new monitor, MSI is now competing with other manufacturers that offer similar specifications for QD-OLED displays. The dual HDMI 2.1 ports will be welcomed by next-gen console owners. Now if you're looking for a high-speed 4K OLED display, you have a more cost-effective alternative.

title: MSI’s MEG X is a 360Hz QD-OLED that can read your health bar — Press Continue
text:
# MSI’s MEG X is a 360Hz QD-OLED that can read your health bar

MSI's new flagship ultrawide keeps an eye on your health bar, so you can keep yours on the fight.

SMEET​ Nov 10, 2026​ All ages

Credit: MSI

MSI’s flagship MEG X is for sale in the United States today: a 34-inch, 21:9 QD-OLED ultrawide running at 3440×1440 and 360Hz, with an AI processor built into the monitor itself.

MSI’s US store lists it at $1,299.99, and it shows as In Stock. The company first showed the display at CES, and Japan sales start in late November.

That on-monitor chip is the part that changes how you use it. MSI says it analyzes what’s on screen without any PC software, so AI Gauge can read horizontal health or energy bars and show their status on the SpectrumBar+ light bar. Other on-device modes include a crosshair that shifts color against the background, a boost for dark areas, and upscaling for lower-resolution content. Visual data for the presence sensor, MSI says, “is processed locally on the monitor and is not stored or transmitted.”

The panel is a 5th-gen QD-OLED with a 0.03ms GtG response time, 1,300 nits peak HDR brightness, and a three-year warranty that includes burn-in coverage. Ports include DisplayPort 2.1a, two HDMI 2.1 connections, and USB-C with 98W power delivery.

title: Introducing Ink 10": Aura’s most compact, cordless e-paper frame | The Full Picture
text:
# Introducing Ink 10": Aura’s most compact, cordless e-paper frame

##### By Aura | November 10, 2026 

Some of the best places for a photo aren’t near an outlet, like the bookshelf in your living room or the side table next to your favorite chair. 

Last year, we introduced Ink 13", our first cordless, color e-paper frame to make it easier to display your photos where cords can’t reach. Now, with Ink 10", we’re adding a more compact frame with sharper detail, three new base colors, and up to three months of battery life on a single charge,* so you can enjoy the look of a printed photo with the freedom to change it in more spaces in your home.

...

Ink 10" has a smaller footprint than Ink 13" and an all-new monochromatic design, inspired by the contrast between precisely machined surfaces and organic textiles. A thin profile and micro-fluted graphite bezel surround a dark linen-textured mat. Ink 10" is dual-orientation and comes with both a stand and a mounting kit, so it can rest on a tabletop or sit flush on the wall, in portrait or landscape.

...

Ink 10" is one of the first frames to feature the E Ink Spectra™ 6 nine-color system. It adds three new custom base colors (off-white, mustard yellow, and orange) to the six core base colors (black, white, red, yellow, blue, and green). Family photos are the most common use for our frames, so we chose the new colors to fill gaps in the original palette that most often show up in those images. The result is more even color on faces, richer detail in textures like grass, and more natural transitions in gradients like a sky at sunset. A higher pixel density of 200 PPI, up from 150 PPI on Ink 13", makes photos sharper.

...

By default, Ink 10" refreshes overnight to show a new photo each day. The slower pace invites you to linger on each image and helps extend battery life, since e-paper draws power mainly when the photo changes. If you’d like to see more, you can refresh up to 12 times per day, or change the photo anytime using the Aura app or the buttons on the frame.

...

Like every Aura frame, Ink 10" is powered by the Aura app. You can add photos from the Aura app, Web Uploader, Apple Photos, Google Photos, iCloud, your iPhone camera roll, or the frame’s dedicated email address. You can even text photos straight to the frame.

Friends and family can be invited to contribute from anywhere, and storage is free and unlimited, with no subscription or hidden fees.

Aura Ink 10" is available now in the US for $349 at auraframes.com. It joins Ink 13" and Aura’s HD frames, including Carver, Aspen, and Walden, which remain great choices for anyone who prefers the brighter look of an LCD display.

*Up to three months of battery life when changing one photo per day. Battery life will vary and depends on a number of factors, including, but not limited to, the frequency of image updates, app and button usage, the light level in the room where the frame is located, the amount of time per day the front light is illuminated, the location of the frame and whether it is in a high-traffic area, and environmental factors (e.g., WiFi strength and room temperature).

title: ASUS ROG PG259QWS Ace: first OLED monitor with 720Hz at 1080p
text:
November 10, 2026 at 3:43 PM Machines › Electronics 2 min read

# ASUS releases 24.5-inch Tandem WOLED monitor with 720Hz at 1920×1080, from $1,099

ASUS ROG PG259QWS Ace is the first OLED monitor to run 720Hz at native 1080p; earlier OLED models reached it only at 1280×720. Samsung Display says it has a 4K 360Hz QD-OLED panel.

Photo: techtimes.com

ASUS Republic of Gamers announced on October 28, 2026 that the ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace ($1,099) and the ROG Strix OLED XG259QWPG Ace ($699) are on sale, according to techtimes.com techtimes.com techtimes.com techtimes.com Open source ↗. The PG259QWS Ace is described as the first gaming monitor to deliver 720Hz at native 1920×1080 on an OLED panel. Until now, 720Hz on OLED required dropping to 1280×720. European prices are €1,149 and €729.

The PG259QWS Ace uses a 24.5-inch Tandem WOLED panel from LG Display. LG's own engineers had called exceeding 500Hz a "virtually unbreakable threshold" because picture quality falls sharply above it. LG's answer is its Dynamic Frequency and Resolution (DFR) algorithm, which manages pixel addressing from panel design through the driver IC. ASUS's earlier ROG Swift OLED PG27AQWP-W reached 720Hz only at 1280×720.

...

On the other side of the market, Samsung Display says it has built the first QD-OLED monitor panel combining 4K resolution with a 360Hz refresh rate. QD-OLED uses a blue organic layer and a quantum dot layer that converts the light to red and green, so each pixel has three subpixels. WOLED uses a white organic layer under color filters with four subpixels: red, green, blue and white. RTINGS reports that Tandem OLED arrived in late 2025 with a four-layer stack and still counts as a WOLED type.
